subject: regexes in test; Boost requires compile

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: regexes in test; Boost requires compile
parts:
Argh, the Boost regex library isn't header only:

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_54_0/libs/regex/doc/html/boost_regex/install.html

I was going to use them in tests, but then just wound up writing
some of my own trivial little string functions for now.

Anyone have any idea how hard the compile would be? I really
don't want to introduce more things that can go wrong and we have
to keep debugging on different platforms, etc. It's not worth
the hassle for what I need now, at least.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: regexes in test; Boost requires compile

What is it you are testing via regex? You could wait until we merge Rob's stuff, run the test iff C++11 = true in the makefile, and utilize the regex library in the C++11 standard. It should work now with your clang++.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: regexes in test; Boost requires compile
parts:
I just wanted to test that various outputs came out
of the parser. I realized I don't really need to match
anything other than a substring, so I just used
std::string::find(), which doesn't require C++11.

There are a few things from C++11 that'd be very nice
to have, such as containers that construct in place
and swap-based copies.

- Bob
